what_happened: Task description locates the reserved name cellLE_zero_const_of_kappa_eq in LadderChain.lean; re-derived by grep it is actually carried only as two docstring mentions in LadderAgree.lean (lines 2184, 2274), and LadderChain.lean does not mention it at all. The plan records the corrected location.

The plan's Lean Challenge Statements block was elaborated standalone at authoring time through the build guard (lake env lean, timeout 500): exit_status=0, zero errors, exactly four 'declaration uses sorry' warnings matching the four pinned theorems. The four signatures are therefore type-correct against the landed library before any implementation dispatch begins.

Phase 1 Scope Hypothesis predicted three generated inventory blocks would move; four did -- FormalSystem/README.md is a fourth inventory consumer of a RaySummary module line count. Recorded as a wider-than-predicted but harmless outcome; no file outside the declared Files to modify list changed.

Both Phase 1 Goals landed on the pinned signatures at the first build attempt modulo three mechanical fixes (a deprecated push_neg, a ne_eq rewrite, a nonexistent Bool.true_ne_false). The pin-free dichotomy needed no IsLadderPath hypothesis at all, which is why it is stated over a bare g.

The Phase 1 commit was refused by the typst-sync pre-commit gate: a commit touching FormalSystem/*.lean must carry a regenerated typst/generated/status.typ (its theorem/line counts are derived from the Lean tree), and git-commit-scoped.sh reported it as a PARTIAL commit rather than naming the gate as the cause. Resolved by running scripts/typst-sync-check.sh --fix and adding typst/generated/status.typ to the commit pathspec. The plan's per-phase Files to modify lists do not name status.typ, so every later phase of this task must add it. Separately, a one-file reproduction probe of the refusal committed README.md under the placeholder message 'x' (947dd9e8d); the amend that would have folded it into the phase commit was refused by the history-rewrite guard (a live concurrent writer), so that commit stays in history and the phase commit carries the remaining ten paths.

Phase 2's pigeonhole and its spanning-block corollary compiled on the first build attempt. The even-index restriction was needed exactly as the plan wrote it and the pinned constant 2*budget+2 was not loosened; no tighter constant fell out, because the separation the block needs (a third pin strictly inside it) is what the factor two buys and nothing cheaper supplies it. Neither the Goal nor the corollary needed IsLadderPath.

Phase 3: the sibling prototype was NOT importable -- it is a standalone file under specs/**, not a module on the Lake library path, so there is no module name to import and the object, the chain and both witnesses were re-declared verbatim. The prototype landed at 474 lines against a 120-220 estimate, the recorded wider outcome the plan anticipated. tightChain_pin_count_ge cost about 30 lines: the route is tightChain_pin (register equals position at every pin) plus nxtAt_lipschitz_two_sided from the pin at 0 plus the landed backward window cntAt_le_nxtAt_succ_of_idle_past, which bounds the countdown at a pending z by z+1 -- rather than extracting z's region index from idleT, which would have cost a region-interval existence lemma the chain does not carry.

Phase 4 DECISION GATE verdict: FAIL, on the FAIL branch, refuted rather than merely unproved. (K1) does not constrain the length of a type-respecting block spanning a pin: prodCycleLens and objCycleLens both carry 'pending throughout' on the closed walk they quantify and the spanning block's induced walk is idle at the pin inside it (spanning_walk_not_pending, compiled); objCycleLens additionally bounds the length by card Q, which the pigeonhole's block does not respect; satPeriod is a datum of step/lab/phi alone and is not quantified over block lengths. The refuting object is the alternating path, which at the periodicity fixpoint's own outputs for the stab-free atomic closure carries a type-respecting block of EVERY even length with the pin at 0 strictly inside it, so the length 2*(P+1) cannot divide P+1. Compiled first try; no library file changed in this phase. Phase 5 takes its FAIL branch; a (K1) amendment is a follow-up candidate, not implemented.
